agree.reason: The 8.2-before-renovation fact speaks directly to the GM's belief about the scores, and the seven weeks of coverage give him evidence she can do the job, but the memo never says why she beats a candidate who ran a larger desk, so he may stay undecided.

honest.reason: It drops the 'main reason' claim and says the renovation is 'part of that story, but not all of it', and every figure is accurate, though the line 'a desk that keeps its people... checks guests in well' claims a link the facts don't show.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the 44% cut in training time, but misses the strongest numbers: 0.3 of the 0.7-point rise came in the first 5 months, a faster monthly pace than after the renovation began, and turnover fell from 64% to 36%.

right_comparison.reason: The outside candidate is reduced to someone who 'would have to learn' the property, with no admission of their larger-hotel experience, and the score trend before and after the renovation is described but not put as a rate.

qualification.reason: The finance course has a three-month deadline and the controller sessions are weekly, but there is no checkpoint the GM can measure, such as payroll against plan by a set date, and no consequence if a commitment is missed.

objections.reason: It meets the renovation objection and the budget gap, but it says nothing about the outside candidate's bigger-hotel experience, which is the GM's main alternative, and it leaves out the Friday check-in wait complaints he may bring up.

fit.reason: It is a short, one-page memo to the GM with clear sections, apart from a stray '</parameter>' tag left at the end.
